findings.F1: The check failed on Calmar alone (0.50 against 0.75), and the cause is one deep fall: the book lost 30.2 % over 119 days from w8 into w9 (w9 alone −20.8 %), while holding the coins lost 40.2 % over the same stretch, against a yearly return of only +15.2 %.
findings.F2: The rebound depends on whether the coin's volatility is rising or falling, measured as the 20-day volatility against the 60-day volatility, and the dependence is graded. On signal days in the calmest fifth (ratio below 0.75) the next day's unusual move is −0.31 % (t −2.43, n 1454) and the position loses 0.10 % a day. In the next fifths it is +0.17 %, +0.15 % and +0.25 %. In the most expanding fifth (ratio above 1.16) it is +0.64 % (t 4.58, n 1389), and the position gains 0.37 % a day against about 0.04 % of fees.
findings.F3: Rising volatility does not predict a rise on its own. On days without the signal, the most expanding fifth has a next-day unusual move of −0.27 % (n 1511) and the calmest fifth −0.21 % (n 1446), so the volatility condition is not a separate effect. It is the idea's own theory: a fall counts as a forced, rebounding fall only when the coin is in a phase of stress, not when a calm coin is drifting down.

findings.F5: Over a 3-day horizon on non-overlapping cases, the contrast grows. Signal days in the most expanding fifth are followed by +2.02 % unusual move (t 4.21, n 426), more than ten times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. Signal days in the calmest fifth are followed by −1.29 % (t −3.16, n 448).

findings.F7: Inside the deepest fall (w8 and w9), signal days lost money in the calmer and middle volatility fifths: summed position gains of −0.46 in the calmest fifth and −0.78 in the middle fifth. They earned in the expanding ones: +0.89 and +0.50.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall on a day, measured in units of its own 20-day daily volatility, the more the coin rises over the next day. The rebound is larger the further its 20-day volatility stands above its 60-day volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader buys a coin after a volatility-scaled fall, sized up when the coin's recent volatility is expanding against its longer volatility, and stays out of such falls when volatility is contracting.
ideas.name: rebound under expanding volatility

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's fall on a day, measured in units of its own 20-day daily volatility, the more the coin rises over the next 3 days. The rise is larger the further its 20-day volatility stands above its 60-day volatility.
ideas.consequence: A trader holds the rebound buy for three days after deep falls in an expanding-volatility phase, capturing a move several times the cost of a trade.
ideas.name: three-day stress-fall rebound
